Hi Emma — thanks for the clear list. I pulled together concise answers below and attached a short evidence pack. Marcus and Neha are cc'd for technical and compliance attachments.

Summary answers (short):
- Prompt & response logs: transient debugging logs are retained for 30 days by default for hosted API customers; ephemeral KV cache entries are kept in-memory and persisted for up to 24 hours only when configured for session continuity.
- Use for training: Redwood does NOT use customer prompt/response content to train or improve our public models by default. Training on customer content requires an explicit written agreement and per-customer opt-in; when enabled we run a strict PII-scrubbing and consent workflow.
- Evidence: attached PDF (SIG responses), SOC 2 Type II summary, and a CSV retention matrix.

See Marcus' note below for details on log types and access controls. Let us know if you need a redlined statement for your legal team — happy to sign.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park

Emma — quick technical clarifications to back Kimberly's summary. Paste below for auditors; I'll also upload the architecture diagram to the Drive link.

Log types & default retention (hosted runtime):
- API request/response logs (full prompt + model output): retained for 30 days for debugging and billing reconciliation. Access is role-based, logged, and multi-tenant data is isolated per account.
- Inference traces (runtime internals): retained 7 days, used only for debugging performance incidents.
- KV cache / session ephemeral state: by default in-memory only, persisted to encrypted storage for session continuity for a maximum of 24 hours when "session_persistence" is enabled. Persisted KV entries are encrypted with customer-separable KMS keys for Dedicated/Private.
- Audit logs (who accessed what): retained 365 days per our SOC 2 policy.

Training policy:
- Default: customer content IS NOT pooled into Redwood training sets. We maintain a strict opt-in policy: explicit contractual agreement + technical opt-in flag per dataset. When opted in, data is processed through the PII-scrubbing pipeline (redaction, token-level hashing for identifiers), reviewed by privacy engineering, and flagged in our lineage system.
- Controls: we provide customers with the ability to opt-out at any time and request deletion of training derivatives; we surface job-level provenance for traceability.

Access and encryption:
- All persisted logs are encrypted at rest with AES-256 and keys managed via KMS. Dedicated/Private customers may use CMKs. Network in transit uses TLS1.3.

If you want, we can carve a short statement for your procurement: "Redwood does not use Customer Content for model training without explicit contractual opt-in and documented PII-scrubbing controls."

—Marcus
Senior Systems Engineer, Inference Runtime
